item.title: FAIR Data - What is an FDO?
item.description:
What is an FDO?

People often ask us to explain what an FDO is in a few short words. An FDO is a standardized and persistent bundle of all information about a digital object that is important for all FAIR aspects of reusing the included bit sequence. It should be noted that the bit sequence can encode any digital information, such as data, metadata, configurations, semantic assertions, and software.

An FDO is:
  • A bundle that complies with the FAIR principles, i.e., it is machine actionable.
  • A bundle that is referred to by a global, unique, resolvable, and persistent identifier (PID). The PID resolves to a predictable, machine-actionable structure (FDO Record) containing attribute-value pairs. The attributes must be defined and registered.
  • Based on minimal specifications. The FDO Record must contain just a few mandatory attributes defined by the FDO specifications, but it allows communities to add their own defined, registered attributes that are useful for their work. Currently, only two attributes are mandatory: the reference to the FDO profile and the FDO type.
  • A passive entity in its basic form. However, many FDO implementations link operations with FDOs, making them active units similar to those in object-oriented programming. In their extended form, they can be autonomous agents that communicate with each other.

What is an FDO not?

We often need to state in brief what an FDO is not.

item.title: About Us
item.description:
Who We Are

We are a team of researchers, developers, and advocates working to build fair and open digital infrastructure.

Our Mission

Our mission is to advance principles of openness, fairness, and transparency across research, data, and digital systems.

Organizing the International FAIR Digital Objects (FDO) Community

The FAIR Digital Object Forum (FDOF) is organizing a plattform to advance the specification and application of FAIR Digital Objects (FDO). The objective is to increase the basic interoperability between the many repositories and dataspaces worldwide and to achieve a better coherence amongst the increasing number of initiatives working on FDO-based designs, implementations and applications in research, industry and other sectors.

item.title: FDOD - Phase II
item.description:
The FDO Forum devoted time to discussing the changed situation and the challenges to be addressed in Phase II. Phase I (January 2021 to June 2024) focused on understanding what an FDO is, developing the FDO specifications, determining where they fit into the landscape of suggested data standards, and developing initial implementations and applications using FDOs.

For Phase II, the FDO Forum worked on organizational changes, redefining its goals and maintaining the FDOF as an independent initiative, as well as organizing annual meetings. The organizational structure has been simplified, and the committees are being adjusted to meet changing requirements. We have worked out a lightweight governance system with more transparency and regular renewal to guide us in the coming phase. Given the increasing number of implementations and applications, FDOF will not give up its long-term plan to become a legal entity. The focus of Phase II was on consolidating and refining the specifications, intensifying the work on compliance checks and interoperability, informing people about the many applications, bringing active individuals together, working on the layered architecture of the global integrated dataspace, collaborating with industry and standards organizations on this endeavor, and addressing new challenges such as FDO operations, active FDOs, and layered architectures.

item.title: FDOF - Phase I
item.description: In October 2019, the Group of European Data Experts (GEDE) organized a meeting in Paris. GEDE is a broad collaboration of experts working in European research infrastructure projects. The meeting invited about 30 experts to discuss aspects of digital objects as they were discussed in the Research Data Alliance, the DONA Foundation, and the GOFAIR initiative. Hosted by the renowned French Observatory, the workshop was titled “Moving Forward on Data Infrastructure Technology Convergence” and aimed to “decide on a joint agreement on FAIR digital objects, stating the requirements for FAIR digital objects, and agree on a governance structure to advance FAIR DO development.” Following the meeting, Peter Wittenburg and Luiz Bonino updated the joint paper on a FAIR digital object framework based on comments made during the workshop.
